To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of 3% FOS to a diet containing either GC or CC did not affect dry matter intake but increased milk production and feed efficiency and decreased milk protein concentration and apparent total- tract fiber digestibility.

flaxseed oil increased milk yield and feed and milk nitrogen efficiency and decreased milk fat concentration and milk and plasma fatty acids profile in dairy cows fed low-starch diets, but did not affect dry matter intake and milk protein yield.

feeding 3% F SO increased milk yield and milk fat and milk lactose yields and feed and milk nitrogen efficiencies but decreased milk fat, true protein and milk urea nitrogen concentrations and apparent total tract digestibility of fiber in Jersey cows fed low starch diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of feeding 3% F SO and CC versus GC to Jersey cows on milk production and composition and nutrient utilization.
the effects of FSO and corn particle size on milk and plasma FA profile, nutrient digestibility, and milk production and composition.
the effects of FSO and corn grain particle size on production, FA profile, and nutrient digestion in Jersey cows fed low starch diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

feeding 3% FOS in diets containing 27.1 or 28.3 % GC did not affect DMI and milk production, but increased milk lactose and feed efficiency and decreased milk fat concentration and apparent total- tract digestibility of fiber and starch.

feeding FSO to Jersey cows increased milk yield and milk fat and milk lactose and feed efficiency, but decreased milk fat, true protein and N utilization and milk MUN, and increased the apparent total- tract digestibility of fiber, but did not affect dry matter intake.
feeding 3% FOS increased yields of milk, milk fat, and lactose and decreased fat, true-protein, and MUN in milk, and increased feed and milk N efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of FSO on milk and plasma fatty acids, milk components, and milk production are not influenced by corn grain particle size.

the addition of 3% FOS in diets containing 20% starch increased milk yield, milk lactose, feed N efficiency, and milk N efficiency, but decreased milk fat, true protein concentrations, and apparent total tract digestibility of fiber.

FSO supplementation to cows fed diets with low starch content increased milk production and feed efficiency and decreased milk fat content, whereas corn grain particle size did not influence milk yield but increased milk fat content and digestibility of starch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feeding flaxseed oil increased milk fat yield in Jersey cows fed a low starch diet.

the inclusion of FSO at 3% of diet DM increased yields of milk, milk fat, and lactose and improved N efficiency in Jersey cows fed low starch diets with or without different corn grain particle sizes.

feeding FSO to Jersey cows fed a low starch diet increased production, but also altered milk FA profile, whereas the particle size of the corn grain had no impact on production and nutrient digestibility.
